Class DevRouter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.dev.http.DevRouter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Router
@Internal @Primary @Singleton @Requires(classes=Router.class) @Requires(condition=DevRouter.NoPrimaryApplicationRouter.class) @DevelopmentActive public final class DevRouter extends Object implements Router
The router of a context in development mode: it forwards to the application's router, the one the context would inject without it (DefaultRouter unless the application replaced it), and swaps that router for a new one when the routes change within a generation.

The application's router builds its route table once, in its constructor, and the HTTP server, the RouteExecutor and the CorsFilter keep the router they received. Recreating the router would recreate them with it, which means stopping the server. In development mode they receive this router instead, as it is the primary one, and a rebuild recreates the route builders and the application's router behind it with WatchableBeanContext.recreate(Object): nothing that holds this router is touched, and the next request routes through the new table. Outside development mode this bean does not exist, so a request is routed by the application's router directly, with no indirection and no check.

The table is rebuilt when, within a generation:

  • a RouteBuilder, an HttpRoutes, a Controller, a ServerFilter or a Filter definition is registered or removed;
  • the development runtime redefines, in place, a class that declares routes: an HttpRoutes or RouteBuilder bean, or the factory producing one, whose method bodies are what declares the routes. A controller method's body is not, as its route comes from its annotations, and a change of those restarts the generation.
  • the development runtime redefines, in place, a LocatedRoutes class, or a class nested in one: the router declares the routes of a located target once per LocatedRoutes instance and keeps them, so a located target that is itself the instance, or an instance held by the routes, would keep serving the routes its previous code declared.
  • a server filter bean, a ServerFilter or a Filter one, is destroyed, such as by WatchableBeanContext.recreate(Object): a filter route keeps the instance it resolved first, so the table is rebuilt for the next request, whose filter routes resolve the bean anew. A module that recreates a filter needs nothing else.
  • a LocatedRoutes bean is destroyed: the locator routes that return it hold the instance that went, and the table of its routes, so the table is rebuilt for the next request, whose locator routes, declared again, return the current bean.

A rebuild recreates the route builders, and with them the tables of the located routes they declared: no table of a LocatedRoutes instance survives it.

A restart needs none of this: the new generation's context builds a new router from its own classes.

    • rebuild

      public void rebuild()
      Rebuilds the route table: the route builders the context holds are recreated, which processes the controllers, the filters and the HttpRoutes beans again, then the application's router is created on top of them and requests are routed by it. Should the rebuild fail, such as for a route declared twice, requests are routed by a router the context can still build, or else by the previous one, whose route table outlives its destruction.

    • hasBodyConditions

      public boolean hasBodyConditions()
      Always true: a rebuild in place may add a route with a body condition, and the server decides once, when it is created, whether it can choose a route by the body of a request. Where no route has a body condition, the server answers as it would otherwise, as resolve(HttpRequest, Predicate) asks the application's router, which knows whether one does.
      Specified by:
      hasBodyConditions in interface Router
      Returns:
      true

    • resolve

      public <T,R> RouteResolution<T,R> resolve(HttpRequest<?> request, @Nullable Predicate<UriRouteMatch<T,R>> filter)
      Description copied from interface: Router
      Resolves the route of the given request among the candidates a filter accepts, see Router.resolve(HttpRequest) and Router.findAllClosest(HttpRequest, Predicate). A FilteredRouter passes its RouteMatchFilter here.

      The default implementation finds the routes with Router.find(HttpRequest, CharSequence), resolves a chosen route with a dynamic target, e.g. of a route locator, and otherwise resolves the routes with Router.findAllClosest(HttpRequest, Predicate).

      Specified by:
      resolve in interface Router
      Type Parameters:
      T - The target type
      R - The type
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      filter - The filter of the candidate matches, or null
      Returns:
      The resolution: the closest match, none, or the matches that depend on the body

    • findAllClosest

      public <T,R> List<UriRouteMatch<T,R>> findAllClosest(HttpRequest<?> request, Predicate<UriRouteMatch<T,R>> filter)
      Description copied from interface: Router
      Finds the closest matches for the given request among the routes the given filter accepts. The filter applies to every candidate before the ambiguity between them is resolved, so a more specific route that the filter rejects, e.g. a route of another version, does not hide a less specific route that it accepts. A FilteredRouter passes its RouteMatchFilter here, so that the routes of a located target are filtered before their ambiguity is resolved too.
      Specified by:
      findAllClosest in interface Router
      Type Parameters:
      T - The target type
      R - The type
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      filter - The filter of the candidate matches
      Returns:
      The closest matches that the filter accepts
